prompts: How do airplanes stay in the air?
Why do leaves change color in the fall?
How does a computer remember things?
Why does the moon change shape?
What is inflation in the economy?
How does GPS know where I am?
How does a microwave heat food?
args.system: Explain it like I am five years old: very simple words and short sentences.

normal.reply:
Imagine a tiny germ trying to make you sick.

But before it can hurt you, the vaccine puts a fake version of that germ in your body.

Your body sees this fake germ and says, "Oh no! That's bad!"

Then, your body makes special helpers called antibodies.

These helpers stay in your body like little guards.

Next time the real germ comes, the guards jump out and stop it immediately.

You get super strong and don't get sick!

The Earth is a big ball that spins around the Sun.
It is also tilted like a slanted toy top.
Because of this tilt, sometimes one side gets more sun than the other.
When it gets lots of sun, it is summer.
When it gets less sun, it is winter.
This makes our four seasons: spring, summer, fall, and winter.

Imagine the internet is like a giant game of **telephone**.

1.  You type a word on your phone.
2.  That word turns into a tiny digital message.
3.  The message jumps from one computer to another, very fast!
4.  It travels through special wires and invisible air waves.
5.  Finally, it lands on someone else's screen.
6.  They can see or hear what you sent.

It's like sending a letter, but the letters are made of electricity, and they fly super fast!

Electricity is like magic power.

It comes from things in nature, like the sun or rocks.
But we mostly get it from big plants that make water spin fast.

That spinning water makes electricity!
Then, it travels inside wires just like a river flows through a pipe.

You can see it when you turn on a light.
You feel it when you touch a doorknob after walking on carpet.
And you need it to play with your toys and watch TV.

Without electricity, our houses would be dark and quiet.

Cats purr because they are happy.

It sounds like a little engine rumbling inside their chest.

Sometimes they do it when they eat food.

Sometimes they do it when they sleep.

Sometimes they do it when they feel sad or hurt.

Purring helps them feel better and warm.

Your cat is trying to say, "I love you."

rows.prompt: How do airplanes stay in the air?

normal.reply:
Imagine a big, fluffy cloud.

Airplanes fly because of four magic things.

First, the **wings** are shaped like airboats.

When they go fast, air goes *under* the wing. It makes a push up!

That push is called **lift**.

It pushes the plane up into the sky.

The engine gives a **push forward**.

The tail helps the plane point right.

And the wheels let it stop on the ground.

So, the wings hold it up, and the engines move it.

Boom! The airplane flies!

Imagine the Earth is like a giant jigsaw puzzle.

The pieces are called tectonic plates.
They float on top of the hot rock inside the Earth.
Sometimes, these big pieces get stuck together.
Or they try to slide past each other.

When they finally move, they push hard!
This makes the ground shake.
That shaking is an earthquake.

It happens because the Earth's inside is always moving and pushing things around.

Imagine a battery is like a tiny magic box.

Inside, there are special chemicals.

These chemicals hold energy, like water in a dam.

When you plug something into the battery, it lets the energy flow out.

This makes your toy light up or move.

The battery uses that energy to do work.

Then, the chemicals run out of energy.

That is why batteries need to be changed often.

rows.prompt: Why do leaves change color in the fall?

normal.reply:
In summer, leaves are green. This is because they have special food called chlorophyll.

Chlorophyll helps the tree make food from sunlight. But when it gets cold outside in fall, the tree stops making this green stuff.

When the green fades away, other colors show up! We see yellow, orange, and red. It's like a hidden painting coming out to play.

DNA is like a tiny book.

It lives inside every cell in your body.

This book has special pages.

Each page tells you how to make parts of you.

These pages tell you how to be tall or short.

They tell you what eyes color you have.

They tell you how you taste food.

Your mom and dad give you this book.

It is your unique recipe for life!

rows.prompt: How does a computer remember things?

normal.reply:
Imagine a computer has a giant, super-fast brain.

This brain is made of tiny switches called "bits."

Each bit is like a light switch. It can be ON or OFF.

When the switch is ON, it means the number **1**.
When the switch is OFF, it means the number **0**.

To remember a letter like "A," the computer uses many switches to make a special pattern.
For example: 00001000 might mean "A".

If you ask the computer a question, it looks at those patterns and finds the answer.

It doesn't use memory like a human does. It just reads and writes numbers very, very fast.

rows.prompt: Why does the moon change shape?

normal.reply:
The moon changes shape because of the sun.

Imagine a big ball (the moon) moving around Earth. The sun shines on it. Sometimes, only half of the moon gets light. Sometimes, none of it does.

We see different parts of the bright side from our planet. It looks like a circle, then a banana, then a line. It is not actually changing! We just see more or less of the sunny side.

rows.prompt: What is inflation in the economy?

normal.reply:
Inflation is when things get more expensive.

Imagine you have a candy bar for $1.00.
Next year, that same candy bar costs $1.10.
That is inflation!

It happens because there are not enough toys and food to go around.
Or maybe prices just go up by magic.

Because things cost more money, your money buys less stuff.
Your dollar is like a smaller cookie now.
It tastes the same, but it doesn't give you as much happiness as before.

Imagine every magnet is like a tiny, invisible robot.

These robots are all lined up in the same direction.

They push things away or pull things close.

This makes the magnet stick to metal.

That's how magnets work!

Your brain is like a busy computer.

While you are awake, it plays games and learns new things. But the computer gets hot and slow!

Sleep helps your brain clean up the dust. It fixes broken pieces. And it makes sure you feel happy again tomorrow.

Without sleep, you might get hungry, sad, or crash like a toy car without gas. So, we need sleep to rest and grow strong.

rows.prompt: How does GPS know where I am?

normal.reply:
GPS is like a giant, invisible map.

It has many tiny satellites high up in the sky. They shine bright lights on Earth.

Your phone or watch looks at these lights. It sees how long it takes for the light to reach you.

The math says: if the light travels fast and takes some time, you are far away. If it takes less time, you are closer.

The phone talks to three different satellites at once.

By looking at where those three satellites are, the phone finds your spot!

Just like finding a treasure by asking three friends where they see it.

Imagine a giant magnet in space.

It is so heavy that nothing can escape it.
Not even light!

If you dropped a ball, it would fall into the hole forever.
Even the sun and stars are too far away to reach it.

Black holes are made from old stars that died very big.
They squished themselves until they became tiny but super heavy.

It looks like a black dot in the sky.
But it is actually a place where gravity is super strong.

Bees fly around to find flowers.
They drink the sweet juice from the flowers.
This juice is called nectar.
The bees carry the nectar back home.
Inside their tummy, they change the nectar.
Then they put it in a special pot made of wax.
They use their legs to squeeze out water.
Now the liquid is thick and sticky.
This is honey!

The ocean is salty because of rain.

Rain falls from the sky and goes into rivers.

Rivers carry dirt and rocks to the sea.

When water hits rocks, it breaks them apart.

Tiny bits of salt fall off the rocks.

This salt floats in the water.

The sun makes the water turn to steam and go away.

But the salt stays behind!

So now the water has salt in it.

That is why the ocean tastes salty.

rows.prompt: How does a microwave heat food?

normal.reply:
A microwave has a special magic box.

It makes invisible waves.

These waves bounce inside the box.

They hit your food.

The food is full of water.

The waves shake the water fast.

When water shakes, it gets warm.

So your food gets hot!
